claims.statement: For every finite bipartite simple graph H, every vertex tag set W, a=alpha(H), and integer 1<=k<=a, tagged independent-set counts satisfy k*q_(k+1)<=2*(a-k)*q_k.
claims.scope: Exact registered bipartite tagged-shadow auxiliary scope, including disconnected graphs, empty W, terminal rank k=a, and integer zero extension; informal proof only.
claims.reason: The origin's finite-set double count is complete: tagged (k+1)-sets provide at least k tag-preserving deletions, while each tagged k-set has at most 2(a-k) addable vertices by bipartiteness and alpha(H[A])<=a-k. A fresh order-245 bipartite forest attains equality at every rank; order-245 connected-path checks show no failure. These calculations corroborate the proof and do not establish the separate eligibility guard or primary aggregate.

limitations: This is an informal mathematical critique with no Lean build or formal award.
The fresh exact computations cover only 122K2 plus K1 with its specified tag and P245 with five specified tag sets; universality rests on the incidence proof.
The separate alpha>=7 eligibility claim remains OPEN, so the primary first-interior aggregate is not closed by this return.
